paragraphs: This passage is about what loss does to a person and where she points her feet next. Naomi, a woman from Bethlehem, sees her husband and both of her sons die in Moab (Ruth 1:3, 5). The passage says it plainly and doesn't rush past it, and I think that's because some losses are just heavy. Still, the first thing that moves her is news that the LORD has attended to His people by providing them with food, and she sets out for Judah (Ruth 1:6).

Naomi tells her daughters-in-law to go back, and she lays out how little she has to offer them (Ruth 1:8, 11-13). Orpah goes back, but Ruth, a Moabite woman, clings to Naomi (Ruth 1:14). Ruth says, "your people will be my people, and your God will be my God." (Ruth 1:16), and she adds, "Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried." (Ruth 1:17). Friend, most of us say "call me if you need anything," and Ruth says she's going wherever Naomi goes, no exit plan.

Back in Bethlehem, Naomi says what she feels without dressing it up: "Call me Mara…" and "I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty." (Ruth 1:20, 21). I think the passage lets her say it out loud and never scolds her for it. But it also puts Ruth right beside her, and the two arrive at the beginning of the barley harvest (Ruth 1:22), so the empty talk, the food and a faithful companion all show up in the same story. Friend, this story is NOT over.
